newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks tumble after sell-off in tech sector.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks tumble after sell-off in tech sector.

text.p: U.S. stocks ended sharply lower on Wednesday after a sell-off in market-leading technology shares spilled over into the broader market.
Concerns that recent strength in the U.S. dollar could hurt corporate profits also came into play as investors rushed to take profits on their gains of the past month.
"The momentum players that helped bring the market up are helping to bring it off," said Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray and Co.
The Dow industrials ended off about 87 points at 6747.

The blue chips had fallen more than 120 points at one point late in the session, unwound by computer-driven sell programs, traders said. The day's damage was most evident on the technology-ladened Nasdaq Composite, which finished off 25 points, or almost two percent, at 1348.
Technology shares were key drivers of Wall Street's January rally, which added almost six percent to the Dow.

But brokerage downgrades on microprocessor heavyweight Intel Corp on Wednesday and fears of slowing growth at computer networking giant Cisco Systems Inc undercut the group, raising concern about market leadership, analysts said.
"The market's run out of fuel here to push it higher," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage,
The selling hit full force late in the session after market heard the widely expected news that the Federal Reserve's policy makers were leaving interest rates unchanged.

Analysts said a larger immediate source of worries for the stock market could be the strength in the dollar, which could hurt corporate revenues at U.S.-based multinationals by lowering the value of their exports.
"If anything pushed people off the fence, it might be the strength in the dollar," said Hugh Johnson at First Albany.

Intel dropped 7-1/2 to 157-1/4 after Prudential Securities and Gruntal downgraded the stock, both citing its price as the reason. Leading the tech group lower were bellwethers International Business Machines Corp, which lost 4-3/8 to 149-1/4, and Microsoft Corp, which shed 4-3/4 to 98-3/8.
Cisco Systems sank 4-1/8 to 63. Analysts linked the weakness to cautious comments by Cisco officials about the company's traditionally weak April quarter.

The slump in the technology sector stole the spotlight from Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover & Co, which announced plans for a stock-swap merger that would create a financial powerhouse with a combined market capitalization of $21 billion.
Morgan Stanley shot up 7-7/8 to 65-1/4, and Dean Witter added two to 40-5/8.

"I think there's probably going more of those types of deals" in the brokerage industry, said Guy Truicko, equity portfolio manager at Unity Management. Such speculation drove up almost all financial industry stocks.
